evidence_titles: 华为与湖北移动完成全国运营商首个 AI 推理加速方案现网测试，长序列 Token 吞吐率提升 372%
evidence_summaries: IT之家 6 月 26 日消息，6 月 24 日，在 2026 MWC 上海展期间，华为与中国移动通信集团湖北有限公司（IT之家注：以下简称“湖北移动”）联合宣布，双方已成功完成全国运营商首个 AI 推理加速解决方案现网测试。 据介绍，该测试基于华为 OceanStor A800 存储与昇腾 A3 超节点架构，搭载 UCM (Unified Cache Manager，推理记忆数据管理)，在长序列 AI 推理场景下，实现了 Token 吞吐率最高可提升 372% 的突破性成果。 文章称，随着 AI 应用加速向 Agent（智能体）形态演进， 长上下文序列 （如代码生成、多轮对话）已成为典型场景，但传统算力卡高带宽内存容量有限，严重制约了 KV Cache 的命中率。华为在 2025 年底重磅推出了 UCM 推理记忆数据管理技术， 打破高带宽内存和 DRAM 的容量限制 ，通过外置存储提供 PB 级的 KV Cache，并对 KV Cache 进行全生命周期的分层管理与调度，不仅在单次对话时大幅扩展上下文窗口，还能在多轮对话中复用历史 KV Cache，避免重复计算。 本次测试在湖北移动现网环境中部署 vLLM-Ascend 框架，针对 MiniMax M2.5 、GLM-5.1 等主流大模型，模拟了 8K 至 190K 长序列输入场景。测试结论如下： MiniMax M2.5 模型场景下：启用 UCM 后，首 Token 延迟（TTFT）优化 26%~62%，单 NPU 卡 Token 输出效率（TPS）有大幅提升。从不同序列长度分别来看，64K 的序列长度下 TPS 提升 58%，在 128K 序列环境下，TPS 提升 78%。 GLM-5.1 模型场景下：TTFT 优化幅度达 51%~93%，TPS 提升 56%~372%。其中在 64K 序列长度下，TPS 提升 313%，在 128K 序列环境下，TPS 提升 372%。 华为表示，测试表明，随着上下文长度增加，AI 推理加速方案优势持续放大，有效解决了长序列推理中的 KV Cache 容量瓶颈。
today_focus.memory_note: 本质是用外置存储扩展KV Cache容量，突破HBM瓶颈，但提升幅度高度依赖模型和序列长度，非通用结论。

worth_tracking.social_original_text:
There are some subtleties in this launch that are very important in practice. This isn’t just you interacting with Claude in a 1:1 format via Slack. In this case, Claude acts as a coworker that any user can tap into in a shared way.

We’ve already seen some agentic coding systems start to adopt this pattern (as well as OpenClaw and Hermes), and doing it for general purpose knowledge work continues to push the idea forward.

As a result, what this means is that this agentic coworker needs its own set of resources, access to tools, and data to work with. This is not the same as you giving it access to your personal resources and tools, because the agent then could accidentally then share those out with anyone.

The agent needs to instead be like any other user in the system, and you need to be thoughtful about what it should have access to, and make sure its information that is safe to share with that group.

When you can pull that off, it’s quite powerful. For instance, by connecting to Claude Tag to Box, you could have Claude access corporate sales materials for questions in sales conversations or generating RFPs, brand guidelines and marketing assets for campaign creation, product roadmap materials and product documentation for coding agents to use, contracts that anyone in the legal team can access, and more.

But this is just the Box example. You can equally have it access your product or customer analytics data, CRM information, codebase, and other resources and agents that would make sense to work on in a collective manner.

It’s awesome to see continued innovation in what the future of work may begin to look like with agents.

There are some subtleties in this launch that are very important in practice. This isn’t just you interacting with Claude in a 1:1 format via Slack. In this case, Claude acts as a coworker that any user can tap into in a shared way.

We’ve already seen some agentic coding systems start to adopt this pattern (as well as OpenClaw and Hermes), and doing it for general purpose knowledge work continues to push the idea forward.

As a result, what this means is that this agentic coworker needs its own set of resources, access to tools, and data to work with. This is not the same as you giving it access to your personal resources and tools, because the agent then could accidentally then share those out with anyone.

The agent needs to instead be like any other user in the system, and you need to be thoughtful about what it should have access to, and make sure its information that is safe to share with that group.

When you can pull that off, it’s quite powerful. For instance, by connecting to Claude Tag to Box, you could have Claude access corporate sales materials for questions in sales conversations or generating RFPs, brand guidelines and marketing assets for campaign creation, product roadmap materials and product documentation for coding agents to use, contracts that anyone in the legal team can access, and more.

But this is just the Box example. You can equally have it access your product or customer analytics data, CRM information, codebase, and other resources and agents that would make sense to work on in a collective manner.

It’s awesome to see continued innovation in what the future of work may begin to look like with agents.

worth_tracking.title: lots of folks prepping talks next week (congrats!). Some thoughts from RLing on thousands of hours of engineer- and researcher- focused talks:
worth_tracking.social_original_text:
lots of folks prepping talks next week (congrats!). Some thoughts from RLing on thousands of hours of engineer- and researcher- focused talks:

- AI generated svgs > AI generated imgs. MAXIMUM 4 ai slop images in your slides, I don't care how pretty your mom thinks they are (exception ofc if your talk is ABOUT imagegen)
- Be pointy. Better to have 1 message with 5 surprising applications, than 5 messages with no concrete examples.
- Put code on screen. Engineers like to see code. Especially if they can nitpick it to death over things that aren't the point.
- Don't forget to Entertain. Being actually funny, or good at telling relevant anecdotes, is more important than adding yet another bullet point.
- Have a Thesis. every talk gets ONE "if you remember one thing from this talk, it is this" card. 1) SO MANY PEOPLE DON'T USE IT. 2) SO MANY PEOPLE DON'T PLAN FOR IT. you get one. use it well?
- Have a Thesis Slide. you've been in that talk where everyone gets their phone out to take a photo of the slide. Because people see 1000x more images than videos, you are much more likely to have a viral talk/slide if you have a single viral slide. You are much more likely to have a viral slide if you TRY and most people do not TRY. Struggling? Collect examples from talks you like and adapt their format to your thing. Your slides have a power law - don't spend 5% of your time each on 20 slides, spend 80% of your time on 1 slide and have the rest build up to that 1 slide.
- You might not need slides. live demo in IDE, off the cuff rambles, pull audience member up to roleplay, do call and response with the audience, sing/perform, voice over vibe videos, I have seen it all. higher risk/effort, higher reward when done well.
- Be pleasant to listen to. Talks with bad/no visuals still can be listened to. Talks with bad audio are DOA. Be confident, project, remember vocal variation, evoke emotion.
- Design the emotional journey. Start strong, end strong, have a peak aha/laugh/thesis moment in the middle. Everything else is buildup.
- Data driven talks are underrated. Present pretty charts and surprising, authoritative numbers. Use the stage authority to infer from the data to support the broader thesis. Done well, it will feel like my obvious conclusion from objectively looking at the data you presented, not you feeding the conclusion to me.
- How to shill your product/company without feeling salesy: teach me everything I didn't know I should to know about the problems you solve, and then you shall have earned the right to convince me you are the guys to trust to solve it once and for all.
- Actively watch a lot of talks. like with anything you both need a lot of reps AND you need to explore to find the styles/role models that you shine in. Passive = no introspection after watching, just mindlessly autoplay next video. Active = trying to articulate why a talk was good/bad after watching. If you want to REALLY hone it, think about how you feel about a famous talk and then TRANSCRIBE the talks and read the words on the printed page, and then compare with a "normal" talk and define rules you will follow for yourself to improve.

evidence_titles: 华为与湖北移动完成全国运营商首个 AI 推理加速方案现网测试，长序列 Token 吞吐率提升 372%
evidence_summaries: IT之家 6 月 26 日消息，6 月 24 日，在 2026 MWC 上海展期间，华为与中国移动通信集团湖北有限公司（IT之家注：以下简称“湖北移动”）联合宣布，双方已成功完成全国运营商首个 AI 推理加速解决方案现网测试。 据介绍，该测试基于华为 OceanStor A800 存储与昇腾 A3 超节点架构，搭载 UCM (Unified Cache Manager，推理记忆数据管理)，在长序列 AI 推理场景下，实现了 Token 吞吐率最高可提升 372% 的突破性成果。 文章称，随着 AI 应用加速向 Agent（智能体）形态演进， 长上下文序列 （如代码生成、多轮对话）已成为典型场景，但传统算力卡高带宽内存容量有限，严重制约了 KV Cache 的命中率。华为在 2025 年底重磅推出了 UCM 推理记忆数据管理技术， 打破高带宽内存和 DRAM 的容量限制 ，通过外置存储提供 PB 级的 KV Cache，并对 KV Cache 进行全生命周期的分层管理与调度，不仅在单次对话时大幅扩展上下文窗口，还能在多轮对话中复用历史 KV Cache，避免重复计算。 本次测试在湖北移动现网环境中部署 vLLM-Ascend 框架，针对 MiniMax M2.5 、GLM-5.1 等主流大模型，模拟了 8K 至 190K 长序列输入场景。测试结论如下： MiniMax M2.5 模型场景下：启用 UCM 后，首 Token 延迟（TTFT）优化 26%~62%，单 NPU 卡 Token 输出效率（TPS）有大幅提升。从不同序列长度分别来看，64K 的序列长度下 TPS 提升 58%，在 128K 序列环境下，TPS 提升 78%。 GLM-5.1 模型场景下：TTFT 优化幅度达 51%~93%，TPS 提升 56%~372%。其中在 64K 序列长度下，TPS 提升 313%，在 128K 序列环境下，TPS 提升 372%。 华为表示，测试表明，随着上下文长度增加，AI 推理加速方案优势持续放大，有效解决了长序列推理中的 KV Cache 容量瓶颈。
company_updates.memory_note: 本质是用外置存储扩展KV Cache容量，突破HBM瓶颈，但提升幅度高度依赖模型和序列长度，非通用结论。

expert_review.skepticism: 测试结果由华为和湖北移动联合发布，缺乏独立第三方验证；372%为特定模型和序列长度下的最优值，不能泛化。

industry_views.social_original_text:
There are some subtleties in this launch that are very important in practice. This isn’t just you interacting with Claude in a 1:1 format via Slack. In this case, Claude acts as a coworker that any user can tap into in a shared way.

We’ve already seen some agentic coding systems start to adopt this pattern (as well as OpenClaw and Hermes), and doing it for general purpose knowledge work continues to push the idea forward.

As a result, what this means is that this agentic coworker needs its own set of resources, access to tools, and data to work with. This is not the same as you giving it access to your personal resources and tools, because the agent then could accidentally then share those out with anyone.

The agent needs to instead be like any other user in the system, and you need to be thoughtful about what it should have access to, and make sure its information that is safe to share with that group.

When you can pull that off, it’s quite powerful. For instance, by connecting to Claude Tag to Box, you could have Claude access corporate sales materials for questions in sales conversations or generating RFPs, brand guidelines and marketing assets for campaign creation, product roadmap materials and product documentation for coding agents to use, contracts that anyone in the legal team can access, and more.

But this is just the Box example. You can equally have it access your product or customer analytics data, CRM information, codebase, and other resources and agents that would make sense to work on in a collective manner.

It’s awesome to see continued innovation in what the future of work may begin to look like with agents.

industry_views.title: lots of folks prepping talks next week (congrats!). Some thoughts from RLing on thousands of hours of engineer- and researcher- focused talks:
industry_views.social_original_text:
lots of folks prepping talks next week (congrats!). Some thoughts from RLing on thousands of hours of engineer- and researcher- focused talks:

- AI generated svgs > AI generated imgs. MAXIMUM 4 ai slop images in your slides, I don't care how pretty your mom thinks they are (exception ofc if your talk is ABOUT imagegen)
- Be pointy. Better to have 1 message with 5 surprising applications, than 5 messages with no concrete examples.
- Put code on screen. Engineers like to see code. Especially if they can nitpick it to death over things that aren't the point.
- Don't forget to Entertain. Being actually funny, or good at telling relevant anecdotes, is more important than adding yet another bullet point.
- Have a Thesis. every talk gets ONE "if you remember one thing from this talk, it is this" card. 1) SO MANY PEOPLE DON'T USE IT. 2) SO MANY PEOPLE DON'T PLAN FOR IT. you get one. use it well?
- Have a Thesis Slide. you've been in that talk where everyone gets their phone out to take a photo of the slide. Because people see 1000x more images than videos, you are much more likely to have a viral talk/slide if you have a single viral slide. You are much more likely to have a viral slide if you TRY and most people do not TRY. Struggling? Collect examples from talks you like and adapt their format to your thing. Your slides have a power law - don't spend 5% of your time each on 20 slides, spend 80% of your time on 1 slide and have the rest build up to that 1 slide.
- You might not need slides. live demo in IDE, off the cuff rambles, pull audience member up to roleplay, do call and response with the audience, sing/perform, voice over vibe videos, I have seen it all. higher risk/effort, higher reward when done well.
- Be pleasant to listen to. Talks with bad/no visuals still can be listened to. Talks with bad audio are DOA. Be confident, project, remember vocal variation, evoke emotion.
- Design the emotional journey. Start strong, end strong, have a peak aha/laugh/thesis moment in the middle. Everything else is buildup.
- Data driven talks are underrated. Present pretty charts and surprising, authoritative numbers. Use the stage authority to infer from the data to support the broader thesis. Done well, it will feel like my obvious conclusion from objectively looking at the data you presented, not you feeding the conclusion to me.
- How to shill your product/company without feeling salesy: teach me everything I didn't know I should to know about the problems you solve, and then you shall have earned the right to convince me you are the guys to trust to solve it once and for all.
- Actively watch a lot of talks. like with anything you both need a lot of reps AND you need to explore to find the styles/role models that you shine in. Passive = no introspection after watching, just mindlessly autoplay next video. Active = trying to articulate why a talk was good/bad after watching. If you want to REALLY hone it, think about how you feel about a famous talk and then TRANSCRIBE the talks and read the words on the printed page, and then compare with a "normal" talk and define rules you will follow for yourself to improve.

thanks to @dexhorthy for organizing the AIEWF Speaker prep meetup tonight. we should actually do more of these....
industry_views.translation_zh: 很多人下周要准备演讲（恭喜！）。RLing 基于数千小时的工程师和研究员演讲经验，分享一些想法： - AI 生成的 SVG 优于 AI 生成的图片。幻灯片中最多放 4 张 AI 生成的垃圾图片，我不在乎你妈妈觉得它们多好看（除非你的演讲主题就是图像生成）。 - 要有重点。与其讲 5 个没有具体例子的观点，不如讲 1 个观点配上 5 个令人惊讶的应用。 - 把代码放到屏幕上。工程师喜欢看代码，尤其是当他们可以吹毛求疵地挑一些无关紧要的毛病时。 - 别忘了娱乐性。真正有趣或擅长讲相关轶事，比再加一个要点更重要。 - 要有核心论点。每个演讲只有一张“如果你只记住一件事，那就是这个”的卡片。1）太多人不用它；2）太多人不为它做准备。你只有一张，好好用？ - 要有核心论点幻灯片。你肯定经历过那种大家都掏出手机拍幻灯片的演讲。因为人们看图片的次数比视频多 1000 倍，如果你有一张能病毒式传播的幻灯片，你的演讲/幻灯片就更有可能走红。而如果你刻意去设计，就更有可能得到一张病毒式传播的幻灯片——但大多数人不这么做。遇到困难？从你喜欢的演讲中收集例子，把它们的格式改编成你的内容。你的幻灯片遵循幂律分布——不要花 5% 的时间在 20 张幻灯片上，而是花 80% 的时间在一张幻灯片上，其余的都围绕这一张展开。 - 你可能不需要幻灯片。在 IDE 中现场演示、即兴漫谈、拉观众上台角色扮演、与观众互动问答、唱歌/表演、配音氛围视频——我都见过。风险/努力越高，做得好时回报也越高。 - 要让人听得舒服。视觉不好或没有视觉的演讲仍然可以……

items.title: Are We Ready For An Agent-Native Memory System?
items.title_zh: 我们准备好Agent原生记忆系统了吗？
items.takeaway_zh: 从数据管理视角系统研究LLM Agent记忆，提出四模块分析框架，评估12个系统发现无单一架构占优。
items.why_it_matters_zh: 揭示记忆系统设计需对齐工作负载瓶颈，为构建高效Agent记忆系统提供实验依据和方向。

items.title: DomainShuttle: Freeform Open Domain Subject-driven Text-to-video Generation
items.title_zh: DomainShuttle: 自由形式开放域主体驱动文本到视频生成
items.takeaway_zh: 提出开放域主体驱动视频生成方法，通过Domain-MoT和双RoPE实现高保真与灵活编辑。
items.why_it_matters_zh: 在保持主体特征的同时支持跨域风格变换，提升视频个性化生成的实用性和适应性。

items.title: Wan-Streamer v0.1: End-to-end Real-time Interactive Foundation Models
items.title_zh: Wan-Streamer v0.1：端到端实时交互基础模型
items.takeaway_zh: 提出统一Transformer模型，同时处理语言、音频、视频的输入输出，实现约200ms模型侧延迟的全双工音视频交互。
items.why_it_matters_zh: 无需级联模块，端到端学习感知、推理、生成和同步，显著降低流水线延迟和错误累积，推动实时多模态交互基础模型发展。

items.title: ShutterMuse: Capture-TimePhotography Guidance with MLLMs
items.title_zh: ShutterMuse：基于MLLM的拍摄时摄影指导
items.takeaway_zh: 构建CaptureGuide-Bench基准和数据集，训练统一MLLM模型ShutterMuse，支持摄影师端构图调整和主体端姿势推荐。
items.why_it_matters_zh: 填补了MLLM在拍摄时指导能力的评估空白，展示了MLLM作为交互式摄影助手的潜力，降低推理成本。

items.title: Improved Large Language Diffusion Models
items.title_zh: 改进的大型语言扩散模型
items.takeaway_zh: 提出iLLaDA，一个8B参数的掩码扩散语言模型，采用全双向注意力，在12T tokens上预训练，性能接近Qwen2.5 7B。
items.why_it_matters_zh: 展示了非自回归扩散训练在语言模型中的竞争力，可能改变大模型训练范式。

items.title: MiniMax：华为与湖北移动完成全国运营商首个 AI 推理加速方案现网测试，长序列 Token 吞吐率提升 372%
items.ai_summary: 华为与湖北移动完成运营商首个AI推理加速方案现网测试，基于昇腾A3和OceanStor A800，搭载UCM技术，在长序列场景下Token吞吐率最高提升372%。
items.brief: 华为与湖北移动完成运营商首个AI推理加速方案现网测试，基于昇腾A3和OceanStor A800，搭载UCM技术，在长序列场景下Token吞吐率最高提升372%。
evidence_titles: 华为与湖北移动完成全国运营商首个 AI 推理加速方案现网测试，长序列 Token 吞吐率提升 372%
evidence_summaries: IT之家 6 月 26 日消息，6 月 24 日，在 2026 MWC 上海展期间，华为与中国移动通信集团湖北有限公司（IT之家注：以下简称“湖北移动”）联合宣布，双方已成功完成全国运营商首个 AI 推理加速解决方案现网测试。 据介绍，该测试基于华为 OceanStor A800 存储与昇腾 A3 超节点架构，搭载 UCM (Unified Cache Manager，推理记忆数据管理)，在长序列 AI 推理场景下，实现了 Token 吞吐率最高可提升 372% 的突破性成果。 文章称，随着 AI 应用加速向 Agent（智能体）形态演进， 长上下文序列 （如代码生成、多轮对话）已成为典型场景，但传统算力卡高带宽内存容量有限，严重制约了 KV Cache 的命中率。华为在 2025 年底重磅推出了 UCM 推理记忆数据管理技术， 打破高带宽内存和 DRAM 的容量限制 ，通过外置存储提供 PB 级的 KV Cache，并对 KV Cache 进行全生命周期的分层管理与调度，不仅在单次对话时大幅扩展上下文窗口，还能在多轮对话中复用历史 KV Cache，避免重复计算。 本次测试在湖北移动现网环境中部署 vLLM-Ascend 框架，针对 MiniMax M2.5 、GLM-5.1 等主流大模型，模拟了 8K 至 190K 长序列输入场景。测试结论如下： MiniMax M2.5 模型场景下：启用 UCM 后，首 Token 延迟（TTFT）优化 26%~62%，单 NPU 卡 Token 输出效率（TPS）有大幅提升。从不同序列长度分别来看，64K 的序列长度下 TPS 提升 58%，在 128K 序列环境下，TPS 提升 78%。 GLM-5.1 模型场景下：TTFT 优化幅度达 51%~93%，TPS 提升 56%~372%。其中在 64K 序列长度下，TPS 提升 313%，在 128K 序列环境下，TPS 提升 372%。 华为表示，测试表明，随着上下文长度增加，AI 推理加速方案优势持续放大，有效解决了长序列推理中的 KV Cache 容量瓶颈。
items.memory_note: 本质是用外置存储扩展KV Cache容量，突破HBM瓶颈，但提升幅度高度依赖模型和序列长度，非通用结论。
reading_questions: 外置存储方案相比纯HBM方案，在成本和首Token延迟上的实际权衡如何？
对于短序列场景，UCM是否有性能损失或额外开销？

expert_review.importance: 这是华为推理加速方案首次在运营商现网验证，对长上下文Agent场景的部署有实际参考价值。
expert_review.skepticism: 测试结果由华为和湖北移动联合发布，缺乏独立第三方验证；372%为特定模型和序列长度下的最优值，不能泛化。
watch_points: 该方案在更大规模并发用户下的稳定性和延迟表现
其他主流模型（如Llama、Qwen）的适配效果
是否会被集成到华为云或移动云服务中商业化

items.social_original_text:
There are some subtleties in this launch that are very important in practice. This isn’t just you interacting with Claude in a 1:1 format via Slack. In this case, Claude acts as a coworker that any user can tap into in a shared way.

We’ve already seen some agentic coding systems start to adopt this pattern (as well as OpenClaw and Hermes), and doing it for general purpose knowledge work continues to push the idea forward.

As a result, what this means is that this agentic coworker needs its own set of resources, access to tools, and data to work with. This is not the same as you giving it access to your personal resources and tools, because the agent then could accidentally then share those out with anyone.

The agent needs to instead be like any other user in the system, and you need to be thoughtful about what it should have access to, and make sure its information that is safe to share with that group.

When you can pull that off, it’s quite powerful. For instance, by connecting to Claude Tag to Box, you could have Claude access corporate sales materials for questions in sales conversations or generating RFPs, brand guidelines and marketing assets for campaign creation, product roadmap materials and product documentation for coding agents to use, contracts that anyone in the legal team can access, and more.

But this is just the Box example. You can equally have it access your product or customer analytics data, CRM information, codebase, and other resources and agents that would make sense to work on in a collective manner.

It’s awesome to see continued innovation in what the future of work may begin to look like with agents.

items.title: lots of folks prepping talks next week (congrats!). Some thoughts from RLing on thousands of hours of engineer- and researcher- focused talks:
items.social_original_text:
lots of folks prepping talks next week (congrats!). Some thoughts from RLing on thousands of hours of engineer- and researcher- focused talks:

- AI generated svgs > AI generated imgs. MAXIMUM 4 ai slop images in your slides, I don't care how pretty your mom thinks they are (exception ofc if your talk is ABOUT imagegen)
- Be pointy. Better to have 1 message with 5 surprising applications, than 5 messages with no concrete examples.
- Put code on screen. Engineers like to see code. Especially if they can nitpick it to death over things that aren't the point.
- Don't forget to Entertain. Being actually funny, or good at telling relevant anecdotes, is more important than adding yet another bullet point.
- Have a Thesis. every talk gets ONE "if you remember one thing from this talk, it is this" card. 1) SO MANY PEOPLE DON'T USE IT. 2) SO MANY PEOPLE DON'T PLAN FOR IT. you get one. use it well?
- Have a Thesis Slide. you've been in that talk where everyone gets their phone out to take a photo of the slide. Because people see 1000x more images than videos, you are much more likely to have a viral talk/slide if you have a single viral slide. You are much more likely to have a viral slide if you TRY and most people do not TRY. Struggling? Collect examples from talks you like and adapt their format to your thing. Your slides have a power law - don't spend 5% of your time each on 20 slides, spend 80% of your time on 1 slide and have the rest build up to that 1 slide.
- You might not need slides. live demo in IDE, off the cuff rambles, pull audience member up to roleplay, do call and response with the audience, sing/perform, voice over vibe videos, I have seen it all. higher risk/effort, higher reward when done well.
- Be pleasant to listen to. Talks with bad/no visuals still can be listened to. Talks with bad audio are DOA. Be confident, project, remember vocal variation, evoke emotion.
- Design the emotional journey. Start strong, end strong, have a peak aha/laugh/thesis moment in the middle. Everything else is buildup.
- Data driven talks are underrated. Present pretty charts and surprising, authoritative numbers. Use the stage authority to infer from the data to support the broader thesis. Done well, it will feel like my obvious conclusion from objectively looking at the data you presented, not you feeding the conclusion to me.
- How to shill your product/company without feeling salesy: teach me everything I didn't know I should to know about the problems you solve, and then you shall have earned the right to convince me you are the guys to trust to solve it once and for all.
- Actively watch a lot of talks. like with anything you both need a lot of reps AND you need to explore to find the styles/role models that you shine in. Passive = no introspection after watching, just mindlessly autoplay next video. Active = trying to articulate why a talk was good/bad after watching. If you want to REALLY hone it, think about how you feel about a famous talk and then TRANSCRIBE the talks and read the words on the printed page, and then compare with a "normal" talk and define rules you will follow for yourself to improve.

thanks to @dexhorthy for organizing the AIEWF Speaker prep meetup tonight. we should actually do more of these....
items.translation_zh: 很多人下周要准备演讲（恭喜！）。RLing 基于数千小时的工程师和研究员演讲经验，分享一些想法： - AI 生成的 SVG 优于 AI 生成的图片。幻灯片中最多放 4 张 AI 生成的垃圾图片，我不在乎你妈妈觉得它们多好看（除非你的演讲主题就是图像生成）。 - 要有重点。与其讲 5 个没有具体例子的观点，不如讲 1 个观点配上 5 个令人惊讶的应用。 - 把代码放到屏幕上。工程师喜欢看代码，尤其是当他们可以吹毛求疵地挑一些无关紧要的毛病时。 - 别忘了娱乐性。真正有趣或擅长讲相关轶事，比再加一个要点更重要。 - 要有核心论点。每个演讲只有一张“如果你只记住一件事，那就是这个”的卡片。1）太多人不用它；2）太多人不为它做准备。你只有一张，好好用？ - 要有核心论点幻灯片。你肯定经历过那种大家都掏出手机拍幻灯片的演讲。因为人们看图片的次数比视频多 1000 倍，如果你有一张能病毒式传播的幻灯片，你的演讲/幻灯片就更有可能走红。而如果你刻意去设计，就更有可能得到一张病毒式传播的幻灯片——但大多数人不这么做。遇到困难？从你喜欢的演讲中收集例子，把它们的格式改编成你的内容。你的幻灯片遵循幂律分布——不要花 5% 的时间在 20 张幻灯片上，而是花 80% 的时间在一张幻灯片上，其余的都围绕这一张展开。 - 你可能不需要幻灯片。在 IDE 中现场演示、即兴漫谈、拉观众上台角色扮演、与观众互动问答、唱歌/表演、配音氛围视频——我都见过。风险/努力越高，做得好时回报也越高。 - 要让人听得舒服。视觉不好或没有视觉的演讲仍然可以……

- You might not need slides. live demo in IDE, off the cuff rambles, pull audience member up to roleplay, do call and response with the audience, sing/perform, voice over vibe videos, I have seen it all. higher risk/effort, higher reward when done well.
- Be pleasant to listen to. Talks with bad/no visuals still can be listened to. Talks with bad audio are DOA. Be confident, project, remember vocal variation, evoke emotion.
- Design the emotional journey. Start strong, end strong, have a peak aha/laugh/thesis moment in the middle. Everything else is buildup.
- Data driven talks are underrated. Present pretty charts and surprising, authoritative numbers. Use the stage authority to infer from the data to support the broader thesis. Done well, it will feel like my obvious conclusion from objectively looking at the data you presented, not you feeding the conclusion to me.
- How to shill your product/company without feeling salesy: teach me everything I didn't know I should to know about the problems you solve, and then you shall have earned the right to convince me you are the guys to trust to solve it once and for all.
- Actively watch a lot of talks. like with anything you both need a lot of reps AND you need to explore to find the styles/role models that you shine in. Passive = no introspection after watching, just mindlessly autoplay next video. Active = trying to articulate why a talk was good/bad after watching. If you want to REALLY hone it, think about how you feel about a famous talk and then TRANSCRIBE the talks and read the words on the printed page, and then compare with a "normal" talk and define rules you will follow for yourself to improve.
